card: Most verbs come in pairs: an **imperfective** for the process, repetition or general fact (**чита́ть**), and a **perfective** for one completed result (**прочита́ть**). Same meaning, different view: **Я чита́л кни́гу** (*I was reading / I read for a while*) vs **Я прочита́л кни́гу** (*I finished the book*).

sections.body:
Aspect is not about time but about how you look at an action. The imperfective looks at the action from inside: in progress, repeated, or simply named. The perfective looks at it from outside, as a single whole with a result.

Think of a film versus a photograph. **Он писа́л письмо́** is the film: you watch him writing. **Он написа́л письмо́** is the photograph of the finished letter.

head: Imperfective (НСВ)
Perfective (СВ)
rows: repetition, habit: **Я ка́ждый день звоню́ ма́ме.**
naming the action, *did you ever*: **Ты чита́л «Войну́ и мир»?**
result still relevant: **Ты прочита́л кни́гу? Мо́жно взять?**
two simultaneous actions: **Он чита́л, а она́ писа́ла.**
a sequence: **Он прочита́л письмо́ и позвони́л.**
no present: its "present" form is future

sections.title: How pairs are formed
sections.body:
- **A prefix** makes the perfective: **де́лать → сде́лать**, **писа́ть → написа́ть**, **чита́ть → прочита́ть**, **смотре́ть → посмотре́ть**.
- **A suffix** changes: **отвеча́ть → отве́тить**, **реша́ть → реши́ть**, **дава́ть → дать**.
- **A different word** entirely: **говори́ть → сказа́ть**, **брать → взять**, **класть → положи́ть**.

Each word page in the lab shows the verb's aspect and its partner.

English expresses some of this with tenses: *was reading* is roughly imperfective, *have read* roughly perfective. But the match is loose: *I read the book yesterday* can be either, depending on whether you finished it. Russian makes you decide every time you use a verb.

Ask yourself: **is there a tick in a box?** If the action produced a result you could tick off (the letter written, the film watched to the end), use the perfective. If not, or if it happened again and again, use the imperfective.

mistakes.wrong: Я чита́л кни́гу и пото́м о́тдал её дру́гу.
mistakes.right: Я прочита́л кни́гу и пото́м о́тдал её дру́гу.
mistakes.why: A sequence of completed steps is perfective.
*Right now* is a process: the perfective has no present tense.

examples.en: Yesterday I spent the whole evening reading.

examples.ru: Я прочита́л э́ту кни́гу за два дня.
examples.en: I read this book in two days.
Have you done your homework yet?

examples.ru: Я до́лго реша́л зада́чу и наконе́ц реши́л.
examples.en: I worked on the problem for a long time and finally solved it.
